title.en: Digital Equity and Media Literacy in Taiwan

narrative_brief:
🧩 拼圖遊戲：建構你的 SDG Pecha Kucha 演講！
透過這個互動式拼圖，你將掌握成功進行 SDG Pecha Kucha 簡報的核心邏輯。

第一步：掌握演講架構 (Master the Framework)
首先，請熟悉 SDG Pecha Kucha 的六大核心脈絡：Part 1 引言 (Introduction)、Part 2 問題指認 (Problem Identification)、Part 3 成果與進展 (Achievements & Progress)、Part 4 解決方案 (Solutions)、Part 5 影響與未來挑戰 (Implications & Future Challenges)、Part 6 結語與行動呼籲 (Conclusion & Call to Action)。

第二步：20 秒限時挑戰 (The 20-Second Challenge)
你會收到 20 段獨立的「20 秒講稿」。你的任務是：
👉 精準判斷： 根據內容關鍵字，辨識該片段屬於哪一個部分。
👉 邏輯拼湊： 將片段歸位，完整還原整場 6 分 40 秒的演說。

第三步：回饋與深思 (Review & Reflect)
完成拼圖後，對照正確答案並思考：
✔ 為什麼這段話具備該階段的特徵？
✔ 優秀的簡報如何透過轉折與銜接建構嚴謹的說服力？

stages.source_description: Introduction (Slides 1-3: Hook, SDG 4 definition, Taiwan context with critical setup)

title.en: Challenge Taiwan’s digital fairness
title.zh: 挑戰數位公平性

A2.text: Good morning. Does every student in Taiwan get the same computers and internet? Today we study SDG 4 on the screen. Our online classrooms look modern, but are they fair?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Good morning. To start, let’s ask a big question: does every student in Taiwan have the same digital tools? Today, we will discuss SDG 4 with a focus on online learning and computers.

B1.text: Taiwan's high-tech system looks wonderful on paper, but has it really reached everybody? For the next six minutes I want to hold online learning up to the light and look.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Good morning, everyone. Today, let’s examine SDG 4: Quality Education in Taiwan through a digital lens. Our high-tech education looks wonderful on paper, but does it really help everyone? We must look closely at online learning to see if our schools truly challenge inequality.

B2.text: Every international ranking flatters our classrooms, and the device numbers are genuinely impressive. What I want to examine this morning is whether a student in a mountain township sees any of that.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Good morning, everyone. As university students, we must critically evaluate the digital dimensions of SDG 4 within Taiwan. While our high-tech educational framework appears exceptional on paper, does it truly foster educational equity, or does it inadvertently widen social gaps? Today, I will explore this reality through online learning.

title.en: SDG 4 inclusive digital access
title.zh: 確保有教無類、公平且具包容性的數位學習機會

A2.text: So what does SDG 4 mean online? Every child should reach the same lessons, wherever they live. But do our schools teach us to stay safe on the internet?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: First, what does SDG 4 mean in a digital world? It means fair access to technology for all. We must ask if our schools truly teach us how to use the internet safely.

B1.text: The fourth goal has always been about fair education for everyone. It should not matter where on the map you were born. Taiwan lives on advanced technology, yet we hardly teach the responsible side of it.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: SDG 4 is about ensuring inclusive and fair education for all people. Globally, it helps students overcome barriers like location. In Taiwan, with our advanced tech economy, we must ask: does digital education prepare us to use technology responsibly and safely?

B2.text: Goal four commits us to an education nobody is excluded from, whatever a household earns or wherever it sits on the map. Our semiconductor economy rests on that promise, although its ethics are discussed by almost nobody.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Fundamentally, SDG 4 aims to guarantee inclusive, equitable education by dismantling geographic and economic barriers. In Taiwan’s advanced, semiconductor-driven economy, an urgent question arises: does our current curriculum adequately prepare us to handle the profound ethical challenges and privacy issues associated with modern digital technology?

title.en: Technology drives education innovation
title.zh: 科技作為推動臺灣教育轉型與創新的核心引擎

A2.text: Taiwan is famous for its computer chips, so schools fill their classrooms with tablets and apps. But the birth rate keeps falling. Do these tools really help every child learn?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Next, Taiwan is famous for its high-tech industry. Therefore, schools use many tablets and apps. However, we must ensure these smart tools really help every single student learn better for the future.

B1.text: We have spent a fortune on classroom technology, because that high-tech industry pays our national bills. The birth rate is now at a record low. The tools change every year, so our priorities need a rethink.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Taiwan heavily invests in technology to drive educational innovation and national growth. However, rapid technological changes and the low birth rate are forcing us to rethink our academic priorities. Let’s identify the core digital problems and see if we are addressing them effectively.

B2.text: Decades of investment in educational hardware produced the prosperity we currently enjoy. With births at a record low and the software rewritten every year, whether that money still lands in the right place has become a fair question.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Taiwan heavily capitalizes on technology to drive educational innovation and maintain national growth. However, unprecedented demographic shifts and rapid technological disruptions are forcing a total rethink of academic priorities. We must identify these core digital problems and question if our long-term strategies are genuinely effective.

stages.source_description: Problem Identification (Slides 4-6: Key challenges, data, and critical questions)
stages.language_pattern: present progressive for trends / this causes ...

title.en: Rural-urban digital divide splits equity
title.zh: 數位落差導致的城鄉網路與設備不平等

A2.text: Here is the first problem. City students have fast internet at home. In some country schools the line is slow, so online lessons are difficult. Is that fair to them?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Now, let’s look at the first problem. There is a big digital gap. City students have fast internet, but some country schools have poor connections. This makes online learning very difficult for them.

B1.text: The divide starts with the connection itself. A city student streams a lesson without thinking, while a school in the mountains waits for a page to load. The gap grows every time the curriculum moves online.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: A primary challenge is Taiwan’s rural-urban digital divide. While city students enjoy advanced networks, remote schools face poor internet infrastructure. This deepens the educational gap whenever schools rely on online learning. Is this sustainable if we want long-term equity for all students?

B2.text: Bandwidth, not talent, decides what a lesson can be. A child in a well-wired district loads a video instantly, whereas a remote school still buffers, and every shift to online teaching widens that distance.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: A primary challenge is Taiwan’s persistent rural-urban digital divide. While metropolitan institutions enjoy cutting-edge networks, remote schools frequently suffer from substandard internet infrastructure. This structural disparity significantly compromises educational fairness whenever curricula shift online. We must consider if this imbalance allows for long-term sustainable equity.

title.en: Fake news threatens student critical thinking
title.zh: 假新聞與錯誤訊息扼殺學生的批判性思考

A2.text: Next, think about fake news. Many of us live on social media, and false stories fly past all day. Few students stop to check them, so our thinking gets lazy.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Another issue is fake news. Students spend too much time on social media. They see many false stories but do not know how to check the facts. This harms their critical thinking early on.

B1.text: Information arrives faster than anyone can check it. Most of us scroll through social media for hours, yet almost nobody has been taught how to test a story. Our judgement weakens without us noticing.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: In the digital world, the heavy flow of information often threatens students' critical thinking. Many young people consume social media constantly but cannot identify fake news or false stories. Does our current system really prepare us to handle online misinformation effectively?

B2.text: What social media trains is impatience, not skepticism. Almost nobody has been shown how to trace a claim to its original source, so a fabricated headline outruns its correction easily.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: In the digital sphere, the relentless flow of information frequently threatens students' critical thinking. Many young citizens consume social media constantly but lack the tools to filter out sophisticated misinformation or algorithmic bias. Consequently, this inability to evaluate digital facts severely undermines their intellectual autonomy early on.

title.en: Cyberbullying risks student online safety
title.zh: 網路霸凌與資安問題威脅校園數位安全

A2.text: Safety is the next worry. Online bullying is growing, and it follows children home at night. Their mind pays the price. Is our school system doing enough to protect them?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Beyond fake news, online safety is a major worry. Many young students face cyberbullying or see bad content. Is our school system doing enough to protect them, or are we just ignoring it?

B1.text: Safety online has become a crisis, not a side issue. Cyberbullying and harassment keep climbing, and the damage lands on a student's mental health. If schools will not act, who exactly is protecting them?
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Beyond fake news, digital safety is a growing crisis in schools. Incidents of cyberbullying and online harassment are increasing rapidly, harming students' mental health. Is our system designed to actively protect young internet users, or are we simply ignoring these digital dangers?

B2.text: Digital safety has quietly turned into a mental-health problem, driven by harassment that follows a teenager home and never switches off. If the school system will not intervene, who exactly is expected to?
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Beyond misinformation, digital safety has escalated into a severe psychological crisis. Incidents of cyberbullying and online harassment are increasing exponentially, jeopardizing student mental health. Is our current school system genuinely designed to protect young internet users from these systemic dangers, or is it simply ignoring them?

stages.source_description: Achievements and Progress (Slides 7-9: What Taiwan has done well, evidence, but with scrutiny)

title.en: Tablets for all bridges resource gaps
title.zh: 「生生用平板」政策推動與設備普及的成效

A2.text: Now the good news. The government started a plan called "tablets for every student". Thousands of country children now hold their own device, so a lesson can reach them at home.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: On the other hand, Taiwan has done some great things. The government launched a plan called "tablets for every student." Now, thousands of rural children have their own devices to study.

B1.text: Now the achievements, because there are real ones. The government's "tablets for every student" policy has handed devices to thousands of rural children. Owning a screen and learning from it are not the same thing.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Despite these issues, Taiwan has notable successes. The government’s famous "tablets for every student" policy has successfully distributed digital devices to thousands of rural children. This massive project provides broad access, but we should probe if it translates to higher learning quality.

B2.text: Look at what the state has actually handed over. Tablets were distributed to thousands of children in rural townships under the "tablets for every student" policy, but a device sitting in a bag teaches nobody anything.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Despite these challenges, Taiwan has achieved remarkable milestones. The government’s ambitious "tablets for every student" policy has successfully distributed thousands of mobile devices to rural communities. While this universal hardware access provides a solid foundation, we must analyze whether high device distribution automatically translates into high-quality learning.

title.en: Free online platforms support poor families
title.zh: 數位國家計畫資助，免費線上學習資源全面下鄉

A2.text: The government also pays for free study websites. A family with little money can still get good lessons at home. That makes the game fairer for us all.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Also, there are many free learning websites funded by the government. These platforms help poor families get good lessons at home. This early help creates a much fairer playing field for everyone.

B1.text: Public platforms are the quieter success story. Free courses have been put online by the government. A disadvantaged family can now learn coding at the kitchen table, and that quietly narrows the class gap.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Furthermore, public digital platforms are very strong, offering free online courses to everyone. This early intervention helps level the playing field, allowing disadvantaged students to learn coding and basic skills at home, which significantly reduces long-term educational disparities between different social classes.

B2.text: The platform side has worked better than anyone predicted. Courses published free by the government let a household with no budget for cram school teach itself programming, which narrows a gap that money would otherwise decide.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Furthermore, public digital infrastructure is exceptionally strong, offering comprehensive free online platforms to everyone. This early state intervention helps level the playing field, allowing disadvantaged students to master coding and basic cognitive skills independently, thereby mitigating the risk of long-term academic disparities across different social classes.

title.en: Broad digital teacher training enhances quality
title.zh: 大規模教師數位知能培訓，提升遠距教學品質

A2.text: Our teachers also learn new digital skills. But when a class stares at screens every day, does the learning get better? Or do they just get tired?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Furthermore, our teachers get special training to use digital tools better. However, we must check if using computers all the time actually improves learning quality, or if it just creates more screen distractions.

B1.text: Our schools sit above the world average for how many students take part. Teachers have been given serious training in distance teaching. But a laptop in every hand can hide how shallow a lesson becomes.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Overall, digital enrollment rates exceed global standards across all school levels. Massive investments in teacher professional development have also enhanced distance learning quality. However, does high hardware participation hide deeper problems, like varying levels of educational depth and severe screen distractions?

B2.text: Participation figures here run comfortably beyond the global average, and teachers have been retrained for distance instruction. Numbers of that kind, however, can disguise how thin an hour in front of a screen turns out to be.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Overall, Taiwan's tertiary and primary digital enrollment rates consistently exceed global benchmarks. Substantial national investments in teacher professional development have also enhanced distance learning methodologies. However, does this high participation mask deeper systemic issues, such as varying depths of educational substance and severe screen-time distractions?

stages.source_description: Solutions and Innovative Examples (Slides 10-12: AI-supported solutions, innovative examples)

title.en: Integrate media literacy in curricula
title.zh: 政府資助媒體素養與事實查核融入正式課程

A2.text: So what is the answer? Schools now teach media literacy. Children learn to spot a fake story and to check where a fact came from, before they share it.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: So, what is the solution? Taiwan is putting media literacy into updated school lessons. Students learn how to spot fake news and use online facts responsibly from a very young age.

B1.text: The good news is that media literacy has entered the curriculum. Pupils now practice checking a source before they pass it on. Most adults in this room never had a similar opportunity at school.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: To address these gaps, Taiwan is implementing innovative solutions, such as funding media literacy programs in updated school curricula. For example, lessons introduce fact-checking tools early, making information evaluation relevant and engaging, which empowers young students to spot online rumors instantly.

B2.text: Media literacy has finally been written into the syllabus, so a teenager is now taught to interrogate a source before forwarding it. Almost none of the adults in this room were ever given that particular lesson.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: To proactively address these resource gaps, Taiwan is implementing inquiry-based digital curricula. The government actively funds modernized programs that integrate media literacy and fact-checking protocols into formal lessons. By introducing these tools early, schools empower young students to critically evaluate online rumors and evaluate data responsibly.

title.en: Personalize learning with AI assistants
title.zh: 導入 AI 智慧學習助手，落實因材施教的個人化學習

A2.text: Some schools now use AI helpers too. The program watches how you work and then sets homework that fits you. Your lesson finally feels like your own.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: In addition, some schools now use AI tools to help students. These smart programs give special homework to each child based on their needs. This makes learning much more personal and effective.

B1.text: More than 80% of our schools have taken up digital tools. Some now run AI assistants that set each student different homework. Those chips come from our factories, though nobody teaches the ethics.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Digital integration is widespread, with most schools incorporating advanced technology like AI learning assistants. These smart programs personalize homework based on each student's needs, connecting classroom learning to Taiwan’s thriving semiconductor industry while teaching digital responsibility in their daily lives.

B2.text: Over 80% of institutions have adopted digital teaching, and adaptive software now assigns each pupil a different exercise. The processors used in those machines are designed here, though nobody explains who owns the data they collect.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Digital integration is now widespread, with over 80% of schools incorporating advanced technology like AI learning assistants. These adaptive algorithms personalize academic content based on individual student performance. This connects classroom environments to our thriving technology sector while simultaneously teaching the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

title.en: Mobile digital vans serve remote areas
title.zh: 行動數位科技巡迴專車，將寫程式與機器人送入偏鄉

A2.text: In the mountains, a van brings the lab to the village. It carries laptops, robots and coding games. Children who live far away still get to build something.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: For example, there are mobile digital vans that visit remote villages. They bring laptops, robots, and fun coding games to rural kids. These programs bridge the gap between the classroom and the countryside.

B1.text: Some of the answers have to travel by road. Vans fitted out as digital classrooms now drive into the mountain villages. They carry robotics kits and coding workshops to the children who would never meet them.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Specialized programs also bring technology directly to the countryside. For instance, mobile digital classrooms visit remote villages to provide coding workshops and robotics mentorships. These initiatives successfully bridge classroom education to practical tech applications, fostering a new generation of creative problem-solvers.

B2.text: Some of the remedy travels by road. Vans fitted as labs climb into mountain villages, carrying robotics kits and coding classes to children whose own schools could never fund either.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Specialized outreach initiatives also bring high-tech resources directly to the countryside. For instance, mobile digital learning vans visit remote mountain villages to provide advanced robotics mentorships and coding workshops. These programs successfully bridge theoretical knowledge with practical applications, fostering a new generation of innovative problem-solvers.

stages.source_description: Implications and Future Challenges (Slides 13-16: Broader impacts, critiques, forward-looking debates)

title.en: Digital skills boost tech economy
title.zh: 數位核心競爭力推動臺灣半導體與高科技經濟成長

A2.text: Why does this matter? Taiwan sells about 500 billion dollars of goods a year, and most of it is technology. Safe and skilled internet users can also help fix world problems.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: This matters because good digital skills help Taiwan’s tech economy. It also empowers us to solve global problems. Safe internet users can work together to find smart solutions for our world.

B1.text: Why should any of this matter to you? Because those digital skills sit underneath exports worth about 500 billion US dollars every year. The identical skills will be needed for data science and climate technology.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: The implications are significant: enhanced digital literacy drives economic growth, supporting Taiwan’s $500 billion tech export industry. Moreover, it empowers citizens to tackle global problems, such as using advanced data science and climate technology to build resilient, sustainable environmental solutions.

B2.text: Everything happening in these classrooms sits underneath exports of roughly 500 billion US dollars a year. The same competence will be demanded again when the data is climate data and the deadline is not commercial.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: The implications of our digital strategies are profound. Enhanced technological literacy directly drives economic sustainability, supporting Taiwan's $500 billion tech export industry. Moreover, a digitally literate population empowers our future workforce to utilize advanced data science and climate technology to construct resilient, sustainable environmental solutions globally.

title.en: Screen time rises internet addiction
title.zh: 螢幕時間與網路成癮問題依然存在，威脅身心健康

A2.text: But there is a cost. Internet addiction is rising fast, and many students stay online all night. Their body and their mood suffer. We have to change that habit.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: However, we still face challenges. For instance, internet addiction is growing fast among young people. Many students stay online all night. We must change our habits to keep our bodies and minds healthy.

B1.text: There is a real price for this screen time. Internet addiction is growing among teenagers, and sleep, energy and family life usually go first. If nothing changes, that damage will follow them into adult years.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Yet, future challenges loom, including rising rates of internet addiction among young people. Excessive screen time often harms physical health and social development. We must actively challenge unhealthy digital habits and build better media consumption environments to protect our students' future well-being.

B2.text: Only when the phone is finally put down does the cost become visible: sleep, concentration and ordinary friendship, all of them eroded quietly. Internet addiction among the young is a public-health question, not a personal failing.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Nevertheless, future challenges loom large, particularly the alarming rise of internet addiction among youth. Excessive screen time consistently compromises physical well-being and social development. We must actively challenge these unhealthy habits and construct balanced digital consumption environments to protect our students' overall well-being.

title.en: AI disruption challenges traditional career paths
title.zh: 忽視數位落差，未來青年將難以應對 AI 驅動的職缺

A2.text: If we ignore this gap, talent will simply drain away. As college students, we should ask one hard question. Are our schools ready for work that AI keeps changing?
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: If we don’t fix these gaps, we will lose many talented people. As college students, we should ask: are schools ready for AI-driven jobs? We need a system that changes as technology changes.

B1.text: If we let these digital gaps harden, a generation of ability will simply be wasted. We are the college students in this room. So we should be asking whether regulation moves as fast as automation.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: If we ignore these digital disparities, inequalities will deepen, wasting future potential talent. As college students, we need to question current educational policies: are they flexible enough to prepare the younger generation for emerging global trends like AI-driven job automation?

B2.text: Ignored for another decade, these structural divisions widen on their own, and a generation of capable people is quietly written off. We are already inside that system, so whether regulation can outrun automation is our question.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: If we fail to address these structural disparities, digital inequalities will deepen, wasting immense potential talent. As university students, we must continuously question current educational policies: are they flexible and dynamic enough to prepare the younger generation for widespread automated job disruption driven by advanced AI?

title.en: Media literacy builds a resilient society
title.zh: 以媒體素養與防詐知能，打造具備抗禦力的韌性社會

A2.text: Good digital lessons make a country strong. If we do not change, Taiwan will fall behind. Media literacy must grow, because the internet will never get simpler.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Ultimately, good digital education makes our society strong. But without smart reforms, Taiwan might fall behind. Technology education must improve so we can handle the problems of tomorrow safely and successfully.

B1.text: A society that can read the internet well is much harder to fool. Without steady reform, Taiwan will slip behind in digital innovation. Media literacy has to grow up with the technology it explains.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Broader impacts include building a resilient digital society through modern education. Without continuous reforms, Taiwan risks lagging in digital innovation. Media literacy education must evolve to meet these complex twentieth-first-century demands, ensuring that all citizens can safely navigate the internet.

B2.text: How well a country resists manipulation is decided long before the manipulation arrives, inside its classrooms. Without sustained reform our advantage in digital innovation will erode, because the syllabus has to keep pace with the tools being sold.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Ultimately, comprehensive media education is the cornerstone of a resilient and secure society. Without continuous structural reforms, Taiwan risks losing its competitive edge in digital innovation. Media literacy must continuously evolve to meet the complex demands of the twenty-first century, ensuring safe internet navigation for everyone.

stages.source_description: Conclusion and Call to Action (Slides 17-20: Summary, strong end, motivation for student action)

title.en: Digital education progress with hidden problems
title.zh: 數位教育雖有顯著進展，但公平性挑戰依舊

A2.text: So where are we now? Taiwan has put a screen in almost every classroom, and that is real progress. But fair use of it is still missing.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: To wrap up, Taiwan has made a lot of progress with digital education. Technology is the key to our success, but we still have problems with fairness that we need to solve together.

B1.text: So where exactly has that left us? Taiwan has built one of the best-connected school systems in the world, and that is real progress. But a fast connection has never guaranteed a fair education for everyone.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: In summary, evaluating SDG 4 highlights Taiwan’s rapid digital progress alongside persistent social issues. Information technology serves as a key tool for our development, but we must make sure that digital education prioritizes fairness and equity for every single citizen.

B2.text: Putting the evidence together, we can see genuine advance sitting beside a stubborn problem. We have wired almost every classroom in the country, although a fast line has never by itself produced a fair education.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: In summary, evaluating SDG 4 reveals that Taiwan has made significant digital progress, yet stubborn systemic gaps remain. Information technology serves as a powerful instrument for national advancement, but it must be implemented through a framework that prioritizes social equity alongside technical and hardware mastery.

title.en: High tablet use screens replace active thinking
title.zh: 挑戰徒有高硬體普及率，卻喪失主動思考的現狀

A2.text: Look a little deeper. Many devices are good, but clear thinking is better. We need students who make things on a screen, not students who only watch it.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: We need to look deeper. Having many computers is good, but thinking clearly is more important. We need to change the system so that every student learns how to create, not just look at screens.

B1.text: We should challenge the comfortable story. Device numbers are impressive and test scores look fine, yet a screen is watched for hours without a single original thought. Deep reform has to start exactly there.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: We have to challenge the current reality. While tablet numbers and test scores are high, schools often overlook the critical need for independent, active thinking over passive screen consumption. Deep systemic reforms are essential to make digital learning truly transformative.

B2.text: What the rankings actually measure is memory and access, never curiosity. Real reform means changing the incentive so that a student produces something on that screen instead of consuming it for six hours.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: We must courageously challenge the status quo of our schools. While device numbers are high, our system frequently overlooks the essential need for independent thinking, replacing active learning with passive screen consumption. Comprehensive, deep structural reforms are absolutely necessary to transform digital education into a truly transformative experience.

title.en: Advocate digital rights and literacy for all
title.zh: 推廣無界限數位權利，落實全民資訊素養教育

A2.text: In the future, digital rights must cover everyone. That includes the groups we usually forget. Ask for lessons that show us how the internet really works in real life.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Looking ahead, digital equity should be for everyone, including groups that are often left out. We can ask for better lessons that show us how technology works in the real world every day.

B1.text: In the years ahead, digital rights have to include the groups that usually get left out. The curriculum needs a proper update. Every course should connect its content to the internet students actually use.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Looking forward, our focus should be on inclusive digital rights for all groups, including underrepresented ones. We can advocate for modernized curricula that integrate real-world media applications, making sure everyone learns how to use technology safely, wisely, and ethically.

B2.text: The next stage has to guarantee digital rights for the populations we routinely miss, and the syllabus needs rebuilding rather than patching. No course should teach a tool without teaching what that tool does to the person using it.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Looking ahead, our strategic focus must shift toward guaranteeing inclusive digital rights for historically underrepresented groups. We must advocate for modernized, adaptive curricula that integrate real-world media applications, making certain that every single student learns how to exploit technology safely, wisely, and ethically.

title.en: Act together equitable digital future now
title.zh: 攜手並進，共創包容且公平的數位未來，就在當下

A2.text: Teach an older neighbor to use a phone, or help a younger student online. Together, we can build a digital future that leaves nobody out. Let's start today.
A2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
A2.workbook_text: Finally, thank you for listening. Let’s take action! You can teach a senior citizen or help younger students with online tools. Together, we can make the digital future fair. Let’s start today!

B1.text: Here is the ask. Join a policy discussion, volunteer for a media literacy class, or simply show a younger student how to check a source. That digital future depends on people like us.
B1.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B1.workbook_text: Thank you for your attention. As students, let’s take action to bridge the digital divide! You can participate in policy discussions, volunteer to teach media literacy, or help younger students utilize online tools. Together, we can build a fairer digital future!

B2.text: So I am asking something concrete of you. Argue about digital policy wherever it is being decided, teach an older relative to recognize a scam, or sit down beside a teenager and check a claim together.
B2.basis: Draft 1 against the v2 quality gate.
B2.workbook_text: Thank you for your attention. As university students, you possess the power to drive meaningful social change and close the digital divide. Whether you participate in policy debates, volunteer in rural communities, or advocate for curriculum reform, your actions matter. Together, we can build a more equitable and innovative future.
